turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. Up on the chair for me and I'll grab a temperature and a blood pressure before you go in.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ah I'm grand. Sure it's nothing, I nearly didn't bother coming.
[SEG0003] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He said that the whole weekend. I was blue in the face trying to get him into the car.
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): Temperature is thirty seven point eight. Pulse eighty eight. Pressure one thirty two over seventy eight. Grand, the doctor won't be long.
[SEG0005] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hello there, I'm Doctor Keane. What brought you in?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): It's just a small bit of burning when I pass water. Nothing to write home about.
[SEG0007] person_4 (DOCTOR): Burning when you pass water. How long is that going on?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm a week... no, four days. Since Monday. I'm grand in myself mostly.
[SEG0009] person_4 (DOCTOR): Are you going to the toilet more often?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): A bit, yeah. Up a couple of times in the night. It's not desperate or anything.
[SEG0011] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any ache in the back or down the side?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Uh lower back, a small ache. I put it down to the van, the seat is brutal.
[SEG0013] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any discharge at all?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that.
[SEG0015] person_4 (DOCTOR): Have you been away anywhere lately, abroad or even a weekend off?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No travel. Just the usual driving for work.
[SEG0017] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He was shivering a small bit Tuesday night. He told me he was only warm.
[SEG0018] person_4 (DOCTOR): So there was a temperature in it as well, even if mild. Any pain in the tummy, or blood in the urine?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No blood. Tummy's fine. The fever is barely there, I wouldn't even call it one.
[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): And the bowels, any change?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Bowels are grand.
[SEG0022] person_4 (DOCTOR): Right, I'll have a feel of your tummy and your back. Soft tummy. Tender just over the bladder, and a bit tender in the left loin. No guarding.
[SEG0023] person_4 (DOCTOR): Are you on any tablets at the minute?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Ramipril, two point five... no, five milligrams, once in the morning, for the blood pressure. And paracetamol if the back is at me.
[SEG0025] person_4 (DOCTOR): How much paracetamol are you taking?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): A thousand milligrams, the odd time. Not every day.
[SEG0027] person_3 (CAREGIVER): They gave him omeprasole in the spring and he stopped it in March. And the statin, atorvastatin, he never even started that. The box is still sitting in the press.
[SEG0028] person_4 (DOCTOR): So ramipril five milligrams every morning, paracetamol now and again, omeprazole stopped back in March, and the atorvastatin was never taken. Any allergies to medicines?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing.
[SEG0030] person_4 (DOCTOR): Anyone in the family with kidney trouble, or diabetes, that sort of thing?

[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Err my father had diabetes in his fifties, my mother did not, umm my sister has the pressure but no sugar, and my brother had a kidney stone a few years back. That's the lot really.
[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): And day to day, the work, the hours, food, exercise, drink?

[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm a delivery driver for a builders' merchant, on the road six till three most days. Diet is sandwiches and a takeaway more evenings than not. I walk the dog around the block, that's the exercise. Alcohol is three or four pints of a Saturday. That's me.

[SEG0034] person_4 (DOCTOR): Let me put that back to you. Four days of burning when you pass water, going more often, a lower back ache, a mild temperature, no discharge and no travel. I'd say this is most likely a urine infection, possibly tracking towards the kidney, but I want the sample before I commit to it.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Sure if you say so. I still think it's a whole lot of fuss.
[SEG0036] person_4 (DOCTOR): We'll send a urine sample today for microscopy and culture. The nurse can take it before you leave, dip and all.
[SEG0037] person_1 (NURSE): Yeah I can do the dip now and bottle the rest for the lab.
[SEG0038] person_4 (DOCTOR): And bloods Thursday morning with the nurse here, half eight. Kidney function and a full blood count. No need to fast. Take your usual ramipril before you come.
[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): If those bloods are borderline we'll add a CRP, that would be the third test. And if this does not settle we'll organise a kidney scan. I'm not booking the scan today.
[SEG0040] person_4 (DOCTOR): If the urine confirms a lower infection I'll start trimethoprim, two hundred milligrams twice a day for seven days. I won't issue it until the result is back.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah whatever you think. I'm not pushed.
[SEG0042] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'll see you back here in two weeks with the results, antibiotic or no antibiotic.
[SEG0043] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'll get him here. He'll say he's grand and forget.
[SEG0044] person_4 (DOCTOR): If the burning gets worse, or you start vomiting or the shakes come back, don't wait the two weeks. Come straight back or go to the emergency department.

spec.situation: Man with burning urine, frequency and lower back ache for four days; fever mild; denies discharge; no recent travel; urine test and antibiotic planned, conditional on result.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

features: self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

bad.reason: Mild fever is mentioned, but patient is not certain: 'barely there, wouldn't even call it one'.
bad.text: Fever (category=constitutional, status=present, severity=mild, temporality=current, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

bad.reason: Caregiver reports mild shivering Tuesday night, but resolved status is not explicitly stated.
bad.text: Shivering (category=constitutional, status=resolved, severity=mild, onset=Tuesday night, temporality=resolved, reported_by=caregiver, certainty=certain)

omissions.text: Atorvastatin was prescribed previously but never started; caregiver said the box is still unopened.
No change in bowel habit was specifically asked and denied ('Bowels are grand').
Doctor stated trimethoprim would not be issued until the urine result is back.
Follow-up was specified as 'in two weeks with the results, antibiotic or no antibiotic.'
